study_identification_part.si4_title: Neuroanatomical heterogeneity and homogeneity in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify neuroanatomical heterogeneity in structural MRI (surface area, cortical thickness, subcortical volumes, ICV) among individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis compared with healthy controls, and assess relationships with transition to psychosis using group-level (VR, CV) and personalized (PBSI, normative PBSI) indices.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Within-group PBSI comparisons (t-tests) showed lower similarity in CHR-P vs HC for SA (t(2642)=-5.39, p<0.01), CT (t(2788)=-9.11, p<0.01), SV (t(2733)=-4.34, p<0.01). No significant associations between PBSI scores (including normative PBSI-Z) and transition/subgroup status or baseline psychopathology; a nominal association between typical antipsychotic use and PBSI-SV-Z (b=-0.84, t(1220)=-2.191, p=0.03) not robust across other phenotypes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Regional VR/CV showed no FDR-significant heterogeneity differences, but PBSI revealed greater divergence in global neuroanatomical profiles in CHR-P vs HC; ~7–10% of CHR-P had markedly deviant PBSI-Z in CT or SV; heterogeneity was not associated with transition to psychosis.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: VR/CV trends toward greater heterogeneity in select frontal/temporal/hippocampal regions did not survive FDR. PBSI scores were significantly lower in CHR-P vs HC across SA (t(2642)=-5.39, p<0.01), CT (t(2788)=-9.11, p<0.01), SV (t(2733)=-4.34, p<0.01). Normative PBSI identified marked deviation in 0.70% (SA), 7.47% (CT), 10.20% (SV) of CHR-P. No significant associations with transition or baseline psychopathology; typical antipsychotic use associated with greater deviation for PBSI-SV-Z (b=-0.84, p=0.03).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Suggests utility of individualized deviation metrics (PBSI) over region-wise variance indices; identifies a small CHR-P subgroup with marked deviations potentially relevant for stratification.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: VR may inadequately capture individual-level heterogeneity compared to PBSI; conceptual discrepancies between group-level VR and individual-level PBSI; inability to control for factors like substance use; variable follow-up durations may reduce power to detect transition associations; need for longitudinal imaging and external validation of heterogeneity indices.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: FreeSurfer versions varied by site (5.3 and 6.0 noted in eTable 2). ENIGMA QC and neuroComBat harmonization applied prior to analyses. Supplemental robustness: leave-one-site-out and exact matching (MatchIt in R). Code for VR/CVR/PBSI available upon request.
